statusDetail: Coverage-complete agentic audit across homepage, search/listing and product archetypes. Checkout/account/payment completion was excluded to avoid transactions and authentication.

page.notes: Public global marketplace with substantial server HTML plus dynamic React-like rendering.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared independent heap summaries before and after ten bottom/top scroll cycles.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Post-interaction heap was 54.70MB vs 54.52MB baseline (+0.34%) and node count +0.24%, with no unbounded growth signal in this bounded exercise.

checkOutcomes.method: Single-state heap summary judged against storefront complexity.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The homepage retains about 54.5MB self size across 609,560 heap nodes before extended interaction, a heavy footprint consistent with the large script graph.

checkOutcomes.method: Compared heap constructor summaries before/after repeated scrolling.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Neither summary lists Detached* constructors; the small total growth does not indicate listener/timer accumulation in this exercise.

paths.description: Homepage and global chrome: marketplace landing, preferences, navigation, network/security, responsive and memory behavior.
Search/listing archetype using a public wholesale query, representing discovery/filter/sort results.
Representative product detail and first purchase step, covering price, metadata and primary commercial actions.
Error-state archetype inferred from the HTML 404 returned by the invalid /sitemap.xml endpoint.

findings.summary: Two simultaneous consent and notification interruptions obscure the storefront on arrival.
findings.evidence: Desktop and product screenshots show a notification opt-in over the header while a 220px cookie panel covers the lower viewport before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not show notification promotion on load. Ask only after a user gesture and make the cookie choice compact, semantic, and non-obscuring.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance to the light capture and the DOM probe reports colorScheme "normal".
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-driven dark surface, text, border, image, and control tokens.

findings.summary: The homepage serves a desktop-width layout on a 360px mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: Layout evidence reports scrollWidth 1280, visual viewport 360, and 920px horizontal overflow; the mobile screenshot shows content clipped far to the right.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove desktop minimum widths and use intrinsic/fluid layouts that reflow at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on the first focusable search control.
findings.evidence: The active input computed style is outline none 0px and box-shadow none.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator and test keyboard order across header, consent, product cards, and checkout actions.

findings.summary: Rendered controls and images lack accessible names or alternatives.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility reports unnamed links and an image without alt; the image inventory found 51 images without alt among the sampled 100.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images concise alt text, decorative images alt="", and every interactive element a discernible native or ARIA name.

findings.summary: Important deal and product text fails WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 57 failing nodes, including #ff7b00 on #fdf8f4 at 2.46:1 and #999 on white at 2.84:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust color tokens to at least WCAG AA contrast and test all deal, old-price, availability, and secondary text states.

findings.summary: Heading hierarchy and focus presentation do not provide a dependable keyboard/AT structure.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports skipped heading levels; the page begins with two H2 skip/shortcut headings and no visible H1 in the recon, while the focus probe shows no indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one descriptive H1, sequential headings and landmarks, then preserve visible focus through overlays and dynamic updates.

findings.summary: The measured load misses key performance and stability thresholds.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 18.5s and CLS 0.238; the trace measured 826ms TBT with an 856ms task.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reserve space for late UI and images, and break/defer non-critical JavaScript tasks.

findings.summary: The homepage ships a large script-heavy request graph before the user acts.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 231 requests and 3.19MB transferred, including 62 scripts / 1.83MB; the trace found four long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit ownership and coverage, remove duplicate/unused bundles, and conditionally load cart, push, ads, analytics, and recommendation code.

findings.summary: The main document lacks baseline security headers and sets a non-Secure cookie.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; cookie aep_usuc_f is not Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP in report-only then enforce it, add HSTS/nosniff/frame-ancestors/referrer/permissions policies, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure.

findings.summary: The first load has a broad third-party and tracking footprint before consent.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture saw 20 third-party origins and Google ad tracking; HAR classified 227/231 requests and 3.12MB as cross-origin, while consent still covered the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential advertising/analytics until consent, minimize vendors and payloads, and batch privacy-preserving measurements.

findings.summary: Sitemap and crawler visibility signals are incomplete for a public marketplace.
findings.evidence: The discoverability capture found only 27% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML; /sitemap.xml returned an HTML 404 page rather than XML, while robots broadly disallows wholesale/search paths.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve representative product/listing content in HTML, publish valid sitemap indexes, and align robots, canonical and hreflang signals.

findings.summary: Most dynamic commerce content is unavailable without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: The crawler screenshot starts with “Your browser does not support JavaScript!” and raw HTML contains only 27% of rendered content words.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core listing/product content and real links/forms, then progressively enhance recommendations and interaction.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bandwidth and omits stability metadata.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 65 oversized images, 67 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 58 legacy-format images, and 50 without dimensions in a 100-image sample.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate correctly sized AVIF/WebP sources and srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold images, and include width/height.

findings.summary: The notification prompt privileges acceptance and competes with cookie consent immediately on load.
findings.evidence: The notification card shows a bright red Allow button and muted Don’t allow while the cookie consent panel simultaneously occupies the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Request notifications only in context, give accept/decline equal prominence, and avoid stacking consent decisions.

findings.summary: Consent UI blocks product evaluation and purchase actions at the first step.
findings.evidence: The product screenshot shows Buy now/Add to cart content behind a cookie panel, with a second notification prompt over product navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the product and purchase controls usable while offering a compact, non-modal consent choice; defer notification asks.

findings.summary: Route/state changes do not expose modern transition support.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition CSS in the rendered document and navigation in sampled pages is a full abrupt swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for product/listing continuity, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The commerce site exposes metadata but no structured agent action surface.
findings.evidence: The probe found JSON-LD but no WebMCP registration; non-JS content coverage was only 27%, leaving agents to scrape dynamic UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Consider narrowly scoped, confirmable WebMCP tools for search, product details and cart preparation while retaining user confirmation for purchases.
